security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, multilingual documentation, normal cache operations, and documented API access. Quota tokens lack explicit restrictive file permissions, appear in request URLs, and lack transport origin protections. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration intent, prompt injection, hidden command execution, or code obfuscation.

remediation.issue: Saved quota credentials lack explicit restrictive file permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Create the credential directory with mode 0700 and a securely created temporary credential file with mode 0600 before atomic replacement.

remediation.issue: Quota validation and balance requests place spendable tokens in URL queries.
remediation.suggestion: Send quota credentials through the supported X-FS-Quota header instead of query parameters, and redact credentials from diagnostic logs.

remediation.issue: Configurable endpoints and automatic redirects do not protect the credential origin.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS for credential-bearing requests and reject cross-origin redirects or remove quota headers before following them.

semantic_findings.title: Quota Credentials Exposed in Request URLs
semantic_findings.description: Quota setup and balance checks put the bearer token in the URL query. Reverse proxies and access logs can retain this spendable credential.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both quota request paths concatenate the token into the URL. The API contract supports header authentication, so URL exposure is avoidable.

semantic_findings.title: Quota Credentials Lack HTTPS Origin Protection
semantic_findings.description: FS_API_BASE accepts HTTP, and default urllib redirects can forward X-FS-Quota headers across origins. Misconfigured endpoints or unsafe redirects can expose quota credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Endpoint configuration has no scheme validation, and both transports use urllib defaults without redirect restrictions. Exploitation requires unsafe configuration or a cross-origin redirect.

content.user_title: Find Visual Styles from Mood Descriptions
content.value_statement: Vague mood descriptions make visual direction difficult to communicate. Feeling Search uses a cached lexicon to suggest named styles and matching vocabulary, with optional paid cloud analysis.
actual_capabilities: Rank visual styles from short descriptions using local word matches, direct style names, and optional fuzzy synonym matching.
Return matched vocabulary, style names, definitions, parent styles, and ranking scores in structured analysis results.
Fetch word definitions, related styles, co-occurring words, and opposing terms through free API lookups.
Retrieve style vocabulary and list cached dictionary words and style identifiers.
Request paid style details and reference image metadata for up to five styles, including attribution and image type.
Check service status, manage quota credentials, and label analysis results as local or cloud.
limitations: Accepts descriptions up to 500 characters; it does not analyze images or generate artwork.
Local results use dictionary matching rather than full semantic understanding; language coverage depends on the downloaded lexicon.
Offline analysis needs a valid existing cache; expired caches currently fail offline, and lookup commands remain network-dependent.
Cloud analysis and reference retrieval require paid service access; credential storage and transport need additional safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Find Initial Style Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find visual styles for this mood: [description]. Use free local matching and report style names, definitions, and matched words.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a short creative brief into an initial shortlist.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Sparse Local Matches
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [description] locally, then retry with fuzzy matching if results are sparse. Compare both results without using paid cloud analysis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: expand vocabulary matches while keeping analysis free.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Style Vocabulary
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [style A] and [style B] using their vocabulary and free word lookups. Highlight distinguishing terms and explain overlaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choose between competing art directions.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Approved Paid References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use one paid image request for these styles: [up to five IDs]. Report image type, attribution, and source links; exclude placeholders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: retrieve references after explicit approval for one paid request.

output: Documented local example, translated from Chinese: matched words include light and white.
Listed candidates include Delft School at 0.25 and De Stijl at 0.22.
These are dictionary ranking scores, not confidence probabilities or guaranteed artistic matches.

output_examples.input: Explain the word cold light using the free lookup endpoint.
output: API documentation example: cold light means even illumination with a high color temperature.
The example associates this term with Luminism and reports its use across 17 styles.
Related vocabulary includes cool white and fluorescent light; confusing opposite terms require care.

output_examples.input: Analyze a description with no local matches, without approving cloud analysis.
output: Source: local. No dictionary words matched.
Paid cloud analysis was not called because cloud permission was not enabled.
Try free fuzzy matching before considering a paid request.

best_practices: Use free local matching first, and approve any paid cloud or image request explicitly.
Keep descriptions concise, inspect matched words, and treat ranking scores as suggestions rather than artistic certainty.
Protect quota credentials, retain image attribution, and exclude placeholder images from visual references.
anti_patterns: Uploading confidential creative briefs through cloud analysis or remote lookups without permission.
Treating dictionary matches as complete semantic interpretation or a guaranteed correct art direction.
Assuming reference images are generated artwork or that commercial reuse rights are automatically verified.

faq.question: Does Feeling Search generate images?
faq.answer: No. It suggests visual styles and vocabulary, and can request reference image metadata from the service.

faq.question: Which operations are free?
faq.answer: Local matching, dictionary downloads, word lookups, style vocabulary, status checks, and quota balance checks are documented as free.

faq.question: When does analysis use the paid cloud endpoint?
faq.answer: Only when local word matches are zero, cloud permission is enabled, and a quota token is available. Reference retrieval is separately paid.

faq.question: Can I use it without an internet connection?
faq.answer: Local analysis works with a valid downloaded dictionary and offline mode. Expired caches currently fail offline, and remote lookup commands cannot run offline.

faq.question: What does installation require?
faq.answer: The client uses Python 3.8 or later and the standard library. A dictionary download is needed before local matching.

faq.question: How should I protect quota credentials and reference rights?
faq.answer: Restrict credential file access and use trusted HTTPS endpoints. Check reference licenses and attribution before reuse; marketplace review does not verify image rights.
